newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-W.Australia to need extra 400 MW power - report.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-W.Australia to need extra 400 MW power - report.

text.p: Western Australia will need an extra 400 megawatts (MW) of electrical generation capacity by 2005/6 to meet increased demand for electricity, according to the latest Western Power forecasts released on Wednesday.
According to the forecasts, electricity demand in the south-west interconnected system (SWIS) will grow at an average of 3.6 percent over the next 10 years.
This will boost the annual (summer) peak load from 2030 megawatts in 1994/95 to 2880 MW by 2004/05.
The SWIS currently has an installed generating capacity of 2680MW and the latest forecast suggests peak demand will increase by 720 MW over the next 10 years.

Western Power believes the new Collie Power Station, an extra gas turbine at Pinjar Station and other electricity purchases will be sufficient to meet demand until the summer of 2002/03. If demand increases as now forecast, however, another 100 MW will be needed in late 2002 and 300MW four years later.
State Energy Minister Colin Barnett said the forecasts provided essential information to private firms wanting to bid for the sale of electricity to Western Power.
"A key step in the reform of WA's energy sector is the introduction of competition into the supply of electricity to Western Power," Barnett said in a statement.

"Through the power procurement process, where Western Power is required to secure any substantial new supplies of electricity through a competitive procurement process, private bidders will be able to bid for the sale of electricity in direct competition with Western Power's own internal generation division," Barnett said.
"The early publication of the documents gives a six-year lead time before new generation equipment is expected to be required in late 2002," Barnett said.
"To meet a commissioning date for new plant in 2002, it is expected that bids for supply would be called during the 1997/98 financial year," he said.
